body.en: When the body makes its own antibodies after exposure to an antigen, by infection or by vaccination, it is active immunity: slow to start but long-lasting. When ready-made antibodies are given, it is *passive immunity*: quick but short-lived. Colostrum gives IgA to the infant; the foetus receives IgG through the placenta. Vaccination introduces inactivated or weakened pathogens or antigenic proteins, so memory B and T cells form. For quick action, as in tetanus, preformed antibodies or antitoxin are injected; snakebite antivenom works the same way. Recombinant DNA technology produces antigenic polypeptides, such as the hepatitis B vaccine made in yeast.
body.kn: ದೇಹವೇ ಪ್ರತಿಕಾಯ ತಯಾರಿಸಿದರೆ ಸಕ್ರಿಯ ಪ್ರತಿರಕ್ಷೆ; ಸಿದ್ಧ ಪ್ರತಿಕಾಯ ನೀಡಿದರೆ ನಿಷ್ಕ್ರಿಯ ಪ್ರತಿರಕ್ಷೆ. ಕೊಲೊಸ್ಟ್ರಮ್ IgA, ಜರಾಯುವಿನ ಮೂಲಕ IgG. ಲಸಿಕೆ ನೆನಪಿನ ಕೋಶಗಳನ್ನು ರೂಪಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಹೆಪಟೈಟಿಸ್ B ಲಸಿಕೆ ಯೀಸ್ಟ್‌ನಿಂದ.

explanation.en: Active immunity: the body makes its own antibodies and memory cells after infection or vaccination; slow to start but long-lasting. Passive immunity: ready-made antibodies arrive from outside (colostrum, placenta, antitoxin, antivenom); quick but short-lived.

title.en: Allergy, autoimmunity and the lymphoid organs

body.en: Allergy is an exaggerated response to allergens such as dust mites, pollen and animal dander; IgE antibodies are produced, and mast cells release histamine and serotonin. Antihistamines, adrenalin and steroids reduce the symptoms. In autoimmunity the body attacks self-cells, as in rheumatoid arthritis. Primary *lymphoid organs*, the bone marrow and thymus, are where lymphocytes form and mature. Secondary lymphoid organs, the spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils, Peyer's patches of the small intestine and the appendix, are where lymphocytes meet antigens. Mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) forms about 50% of the lymphoid tissue in the body.
body.kn: ಅಲರ್ಜಿಯಲ್ಲಿ IgE ಉತ್ಪತ್ತಿಯಾಗಿ ಮಾಸ್ಟ್ ಕೋಶಗಳು ಹಿಸ್ಟಮಿನ್ ಬಿಡುಗಡೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಸ್ವಪ್ರತಿರಕ್ಷೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ದೇಹ ತನ್ನ ಕೋಶಗಳ ಮೇಲೆ ದಾಳಿ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ ಲಿಂಫಾಯ್ಡ್ ಅಂಗಗಳು: ಮೂಳೆ ಮಜ್ಜೆ, ಥೈಮಸ್; ದ್ವಿತೀಯ: ಗುಲ್ಮ, ದುಗ್ಧರಸ ಗ್ರಂಥಿಗಳು, ಟಾನ್ಸಿಲ್‌ಗಳು, ಪೇಯರ್ಸ್ ಪ್ಯಾಚ್‌ಗಳು.

points.en: Secondary: spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils, Peyer's patches, appendix; MALT ~50%

problem.en: Classify each as active or passive immunity: (a) a child receives the polio vaccine; (b) a snakebite victim receives antivenom; (c) a baby drinks colostrum; (d) a person recovers from measles.

steps.en: Active immunity means the person's own body makes antibodies: (a) vaccine and (d) natural infection.
Passive immunity means ready-made antibodies are received: (b) antivenom and (c) IgA in colostrum.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Classify each as active or passive immunity: a a child receives the polio vaccine; b a snakebite victim receives antivenom; c a baby drinks colostrum; d a person recovers from measles.
Active immunity means the person's own body makes antibodies: a vaccine and d natural infection.
Passive immunity means ready-made antibodies are received: b antivenom and c IgA in colostrum.
So the answer is a Active b Passive c Passive d Active.
